We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-2.18<Z<2.18).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/fb6af7fb416087d41fb826260cca7b504a599f2aa44a90e65f8fe2fc3ffaac43.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.18<Z<2.18) & =P(Z<2.18)-P(Z\le -2.18) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.18)-P(Z\le -2.18) \\  & =Φ(2.18)-Φ(-2.18)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-2.18)=0.0146,
$$

but we are not given $Φ(2.18).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.18) & =P(Z\le 2.18) \\  & =P(Z\ge -2.18) \\  & =1-P(Z<-2.18) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -2.18) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.18) \\  & =1-0.0146 \\  & =0.9854\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.18<Z<2.18) & =Φ(2.18)-Φ(-2.18) \\  & =0.9854-0.0146 \\  & =0.9708.\end{aligned}
$$
